Guide & Academy/BA Lending Academy/Module 13

Module 13 of 15

Business analysis practice for lending

Convert regulation and product intent into testable states, data, controls and operational readiness.

Domain knowledge is not enough. These lessons provide the BA work products and reasoning patterns needed to deliver a regulated lending change without losing failure paths, evidence, ownership or production boundaries.

Lesson 13.1 · 24 min

Problem framing, scope and stakeholders

  • Write an outcome-based problem statement
  • Map decision owners and affected actors
  • Control assumptions and scope boundaries

Lesson 13.2 · 24 min

Process maps, state machines and exceptions

  • Model actors, events and states separately
  • Specify guards and restrictive failure paths
  • Cover timeout, retry, cancellation and repair

Lesson 13.3 · 24 min

Data, rules, lineage and migration

  • Write a field-level data contract
  • Separate source facts from derived decisions
  • Design migration and reconciliation

Lesson 13.4 · 24 min

Controls, roles and evidence requirements

  • Turn an obligation into preventive and detective controls
  • Specify segregation and authority
  • Define evidence and operating-effectiveness tests

Lesson 13.5 · 24 min

Acceptance criteria, test design and UAT

  • Write rule and state-based acceptance criteria
  • Build positive, negative and boundary cases
  • Separate platform verification from tenant UAT

Lesson 13.6 · 24 min

Change impact, rollout and post-release control

  • Assess impact across process, data, policy and operations
  • Design migration, training and rollback
  • Define production admission and monitoring
